knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The scope depends on owner approval, the surface, the exclusions and whether a specialist or licensed contractor is needed. A pressure cleaner is not the default.
Extra work not in an accepted quote needs the customer's approval first [WA-QUOTE][NT-QUOTE].
Stopping, keeping people clear and reporting before work near an electrical hazard is the stop-work and referral rule in this lesson.

practicalCriteria: Completes a scope record for a sample site showing the address, surfaces, drains, people, vehicles, landscaping, restrictions, exclusions and written owner approval, checked by the assessor against a checklist.
Marks the excluded zones on a sample site plan, and states which items need a licensed contractor or specialist, with a reason for each.
Writes an extra-work request for a sample scope change, and shows that the work is held until approval is recorded.
passRule: Assessor review of the scope record, site plan and extra-work request for the sample site, with all three practical criteria met. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Scope record with written owner approval
Annotated site plan with excluded zones
Extra-work request with the approval or refusal recorded
stopWorkCriteria: Work starts before the owner's written scope is on file
Roof, height or electrical work is included in the scope without authorisation
Regulated jetting or Class B equipment is requested
A surface, electrical hazard or exclusion zone is uncertain and work continues
